comparison.objective: Candidate sets and locks a gripper stop; PR-793 twists a rubber stopper onto a glass tube safely.
comparison.physical_skill: Both involve bimanual rotational work, but the candidate counterholds an adjustment screw while tightening a concentric jam nut; PR-793 holds fragile glass near the work while twisting and pushing an interference-fit stopper.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires a locked target angle retained through three cycles; PR-793 requires at least 12 mm insertion, release, and no unsafe unsupported working action.
comparison.reason: The closest shared primitive is counterholding, but only the candidate tests preserving a calibrated setting during independent locknut tightening and subsequent actuation.
